Round 3940.decision_summary: The two carries of round 3939 are paid, and neither is moved forward. (1) Whether a Put is sent or read plain was a fact of the BUILD: any build that compiled routing-namespace or transport-stats sent and read no plain Put at all, so since router-node enables routing-namespace a whole workspace build lost the lane, for sessions that hold no namespace and count nothing differently. The textbook partition is the one the egress policy already followed (Session::plain_put_lane_open): what can stop a plain Put is a fact about the SESSION, asked where it is sent. A namespace rewrites the key of each message a session originates, which the owned send does, so SessionLinkActions::send_plain_put_qos answers None for a session that holds one (rewrites_originated_keys, shared with the reply-from-parts gate) and every caller sends the owned message then; the tokio lane gate, the C ABI fan-out (which asks every face before it sends to any, so a put goes plain to all or to none) and the cooperative engine read the same answer. The network counters no longer need the owned message: a plain Put sent or received is classed by plain_put_stats_class, which shares the key-space rule with the owned Push's class (stats_space_of_key) and is held equal to it by a test over literal and aliased, user and admin keys, and its band by the one ext_qos rule (qos_of_raw); the lend-only literal send counts the same way. PublishOptions::plain_put_params and SENDS_PLAIN_PUTS now depend on the Push codec alone, and the coop filter tests return to their strict form. (2) The scouting-active reason's anchor names the fan-out test by its in_a_netns_ name, set through the typed inventory primitive.

Round 3944.decision_summary:
The line table of the answering client's image put the largest lines of its own code in the two calls of a critical section: 127 calls of `wz_irq_lock` and 142 of `wz_irq_unlock`, 33 of the first in `SessionActionsBinding`, 20 in `SessionLinkActions`, 14 in `decide_unit_in`. Each is a borrow of a `critical_section::Mutex<RefCell<T>>` cell, a call to the kernel's `irq_lock` and back around the `RefCell`'s flag, and the guard exists for an interrupt handler or another thread that reaches the same cell.

`wz-runtime-coop` has a feature `single-context` in which `cs::with`, the one door every lock of the crate goes through, hands out the token without masking interrupts; the Zephyr node selects it with `CONFIG_WZ_SINGLE_CONTEXT` (off by default; the T2G overlay turns it on). The image states the contract the lock was for the want of: its Rust has no interrupt handler, timer or thread, and the Ethernet driver's threads call the MAC in `zeth_exports.rs` and nothing of the runtime, so the node's thread is the only caller. A board that feeds the loop from an interrupt through the runtime's cells leaves it off. The cell types and the `RefCell` borrow rules are unchanged; a test holds that a section still runs its closure once, nests, and refuses a re-entrant borrow.

The kit text fell 1,352 bytes on the fixed image (147,556 to 146,204), 2,280 on the batching (151,684 to 149,404) and 1,304 on the get image (165,164 to 163,860); the worst stack chain fell 2,616 to 2,560, the bound 3,352 to 3,296 and the kit's peak 2,696 to 2,672. The text and stack rows are moved to those figures. The same build found that the line-pinned rule `entropy-draw` of `deploy/stack_call_contracts.json` named `session_actions.rs:6148` while the call sits at 6169 (the rebase onto the commits other sessions had pushed moved it), which the stack bound refused for every image; the pin is 6169.

Round 3944's ledger commit (`2244962db0`) moved the `vendor/sce` pointer from b1ede72108 to 6dbfa6a521. This commit puts the pointer back at b1ede72108. The cause is in how a worktree lands: after the rebase onto commits that moved the pin, the submodule checkout of the worktree is behind the index and the ledger commit takes the checkout. The worktree's submodule is brought to the rebased pin before the round is filed from now on.

The SCE pin `b1ede72108` that another session took in `69bc0b0e0b` (ADR 0065: the codecs that may refuse an encode return a `Result`) holds ADR 0064's shared engine core below it, which the SCE owner had asked consumers not to take until it is smaller than the copies it replaces. The kit lane is not run by any hook, so the commit landed with the kit gates red. Read at origin's main, the three images: the text 149,336, 152,512 and 168,624 (Round 3944's rows: 146,204, 149,404, 163,860), the worst chain of direct calls 2,560 to 2,740, the bound 3,296 to 3,764 on the fixed and batching images (over three quarters of the 4,480-byte stack) and the kit's peak 2,672 to 3,000.

The stack bound also met call sites no rule claimed: the shared copy of Appendix D reaches the machine it drives through a reference to the engine's `MainLoop` and `Behaviour`. Two rules state it, one for the file of each trait (`engine-host` for `engine.rs`, `engine-behaviour` for `microstep.rs`), each limited to the methods of its trait, with the number of sites pinned for each image (21 and 11); the line of `engine-clock` and of the two `tx_buf.rs` rules moved with the pins. The main stack of the fixed and batching overlays is 5,056 bytes, a quarter free over the bound.

The rows (the text and owners, the chain, the bound, the peak) are moved to those readings with the reason, so that the gates hold again and a later change is read against the pin it was made on. The cost is SCE's to take out: its owner works on the shells of the machines and on the core, and sends a commit when its probe shows two machines below the old size; the rows and the stack follow it down. The other session was told.

Round 3954.decision_summary: A get routed through a node whose peer is hosted in the same forwarder could wait out its timeout, whatever answered it. The last branch of a query was told by the strong count of the Arc of its fan, and the routing call holds a handle of its own while it sends the branches: a final that came back in that window (a link answers within microseconds, and a loaded machine lengthens the window) found the handle, was told it was not the last and was absorbed, and the call then let go of the fan with no branch left to send the closing final. The pin sends its branches after it has dropped its hold, so its gate is sound there; wz keeps the hold during the sends. The fan now counts its live holders, the routing call being one of them, and the call lets go of its own once the branches are sent: whoever takes the count to zero sends the final, which is one holder from any number of tasks, in any order.

Round 3955.decision_summary:
The Request body's Put and Del arms leave the images of the zenoh preset. Pinned zenoh 1.10.1 accepts only a Query as a request body (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/zenoh/mod.rs` @ `id::QUERY => RequestBody::Query`); zenoh-pico's decoder takes the Query, the Put and the Del, and that is the pico preset's contract, so the arms stay in every build that does not say otherwise. SCE ADR 0072 (`vendor/sce` 44e6d3083b) lets a variant arm name a build feature: `sources/codecs/request.scxml` names `request-put-del` on the two arms, `wz-codecs` declares it (on by default), `wz-session-core` forwards it (on by default) and compiles the code that judges a Put's or Del's extension chains only with it. With it off a Put or Del tag under a Request is refused by the decoder (`CodecError::VariantArmNotBuilt`) and does not reach the catch-all, and the decoders of the two bodies, which only the Request decode reached in the answering client, are not linked (their symbols are not in the image).

The Zephyr node reads it from `CONFIG_WZ_REQUEST_PUT_DEL` (Kconfig, default `y`, so every other board and image is as it was); `overlays/t2g_client_fixed.conf`, which the batching, get and TLS overlays are chained on, sets it off. The crates that named the variants or ask for `codec-request` without the session-core default now ask for the feature too (`wz-capture`, `wz-capi-coop`, `wz-ext-pubsub`); `cargo tree` over the 89 packages of `crates/` found no other graph that has `codec-request` on and the feature off. Where the codec builds the arms and session-core's feature is off (a graph that mixes the two), session-core judges such a body `Unjudged` and the code compiles, so a mixed graph does not fail on a non-exhaustive match.

Round 3962.decision_summary:
The stack contract stops counting an edge that the code of the entry walk cannot take. The SCE owner pointed at it after the bound of the fixed and batching images was read: `walk_entry`, `effective_target_states_on` and `is_in_final_state` (`vendor/sce` backends/rust/runtime/src/helpers/microstep.rs) take the document's tables, the store and sets, and no `Behaviour`; their four calls through a register are the history and parallel procedures read from the tables (`HISTORY`, `PARALLEL`), which a document without a `<history>` and a `<parallel>` (both of the node's documents) does not carry. The Behaviour hooks are called from `enter_states`, beside the walk and not under it, and the contract had charged the walk's 112-byte frame under the hook's. The rule `walk-entry-tables` claims those four sites as calling nothing, with the premise stated and checked by the gate: no function of the image is one of the seven procedures of the two tables (a first, wider form of the premise matched the Behaviour hook `execute_history_default_content` and was refused by the gate itself; it names the seven now). `engine-behaviour` pins 13 sites where it pinned 17.

The get image's worst path is another one and its bound stays 4,564. The chain (2,536), the kit's peak (2,912), the text and the runs, which are what the image holds and does, did not move: this is the proof getting nearer to the code and not a change of the code, and it does not touch the `stack_used` cell, which is the peak.

The SCE owner has no change left for `enter_states`, `walk_entry` or `Turn::run` (the one lever, computing the entry set out of line, measured 760 to 856 bytes of worst-case stack in its probe), so the 137 bytes `stack_used` needs are in the node's own frames (`reconcile` 448, the loop 392, the binding's action 288).

Round 3964.decision_summary:
The kit's stack reading is read from what the console prints, and three frames of the node came down by looking at what that reading is made of. The image prints `stack: peak N of M bytes` when the high-water mark rises: once at READY (the dial) and once more after "session established". The second figure was 2,896 bytes and no change to the path that answers a query moved it, because it is not that path: it is the receive of the router's handshake message. This was found by taking the deepest path through each function of the call graph (the bound gate's graph, now carried out of the gate in `Result`, and a script that groups the paths) and then by changing a frame on a path and reading whether the console moved: `reconcile` moved the READY figure by exactly 120 bytes and the second by none; a deferral of the reply send to the end of the datagram's receive took 628 bytes off the query path and moved nothing, and was dropped for the 300 bytes of text it cost.

What moved it: (1) the receive's reading of a handshake message is its own function, `read_unit_in`, out of line from `dispatch_unit_in`, which gives the engine the event of the admitted message once the 400-byte slot of the decoded message is gone; the engine's answer writes and sends the next handshake message, the deepest call of the receive, and the slot was under it though nothing read it (the second figure 2,928 to 2,720 in the run measured); (2) `reconcile` orders the connect manager's rows by swaps of neighbours and not by `rotate_right(1)`, whose library code inlined a row (152 bytes) and a buffer of its own: 448 bytes of frame to 328, the chain 2,536 to 2,416, the bound 3,476 to 3,356 and the main stack of the fixed and batching overlays 4,672 to 4,480 bytes, 192 bytes of `.bss`; (3) `log_parts` and `log_args` fill one buffer and no longer take one back by value (832 bytes of frame, the largest of the image, under every log line, to under 736).

Round 3978.decision_summary: A zenohd oracle is a fact about a machine, and it was stored as a fact about one checkout. build-zenohd.sh cloned, built and installed into the checkout's own target/, and a build machine runs this repository in several checkout slots, each with its own target/: on 2026-10-30 slot 1 of a build machine held a zenohd at the pin after an 11-minute build from the pinned tag, and the next run, placed in slot 2, found none (oracle-pin-gate ABSENT four times). That is not a defect of the build fleet's tool, whose slots are interchangeable by contract; the tree put a machine-level artifact in a per-checkout place. Oracles are now built once per machine into a store that scripts/lib/oracle_store.py derives ($WZ_ORACLE_STORE, else the XDG cache), keyed by version and by the digest of build-zenohd.sh, which alone decides an oracle's contents. target/zenohd* stays a real directory that every consumer reads, materialized from the store by copy rather than linked, because the hosted job caches and archives those directories with tar. Only an oracle that answers with the pin is published, judged by oracle_pin_gate.inspect, so the store cannot hold what the gate calls STALE; for the same reason build-zenohd.sh now refuses a source tree that cannot name the pin instead of warning and building an oracle the gate rejects. Round 3991.decision_summary:
The SCE pin moves to dc579571aa (ADR 0076: a Rust machine has an internal and an external queue type, and the internal queue is sized by the depth the generator proves from the document). For both of the client's documents the proven depth is 0, as the session document has no `<raise>`, no `<send>`, no `<donedata>` and no fallible guard, and its only `<final>` is top-level: nothing it does can put an event on that queue, and a build with debug assertions holds every raise to the proof. The external queue is the host's statement, and the host gives the session machine one event at a time (`process_event` runs it to the end before it returns), so `sce:capacity` of `sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml` is 2, as the peer document's is, where it was 16 (and 64 before that, in a queue pair of 272 bytes each). The heap client's storage block is 8,224 bytes, from 8,384 (11,568 before the client stated what it carries); the fixed image's .bss fell 160 bytes and its text 48.

Round 3998.decision_summary: A node's link-state flood (a face coming up, a topology list taken in, the tick) went out inside the node's tables, on the one loop that serves every face, and a send that found the link without room waited for it there, up to wait_before_close (5 s): measured as 71 sends of 4.9 to 5.0 s over 960 recipes of upstream's routing test, each holding a face's registration and the dial that answered it. Nobody can be told to slow down for a control message, so the answer is not the publisher's wait of the previous round but the credit stage's: a reliable link-state message that finds no room is held, whole, in a queue of its destination, in order, and leaves when the link has room. The queue is the control lane's, apart from the data lane's, so control does not wait behind data; it gates no face (two routers that stopped reading each other would wait for ever); the age of its oldest message bounds it, as for data.

Round 4003.decision_summary: The cooperative engine's tls/ link was carried as a build that selects the tokio engine by design. Reading the tree showed that is not the whole story and that the obvious composition does not work: wz-tls-mbedtls already is a StreamSocket and a StreamDial, but it is TLS 1.3 with one suite and no PEM reader, and it accepts a peer by the zid of its key (VERIFY_OPTIONAL, no host name, decision D1), while pico's tls/ and zenohd's verify a CA chain, present a chain and key under mTLS, and check the name only on request. The design is filed as step L6 of docs/capi-pico-on-coop-engine.md: the trust policy is a parameter of the one channel, Pinned (what exists, still the default) and Chain (roots, name check, own chain and key as PEM); the seam stays StreamDial; pico's keys resolve once for both engines; a feature picks the provider. A rustls provider in the cooperative engine was refused because it leaves the MCU line without TLS. Steps T1 to T5 each state their proof. Nothing is built.
